title: Statutes (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill debated and read a Third time
what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, the Statutes (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill, making miscellaneous amendments to several Acts, including BCA, URA, COTMA, Architects Act, Professional Engineers Act, HDB Act, Wildlife Act and Endangered Species Act.
stage: Second Reading, Committee stage, and Third Reading
why_it_matters: The record says the Bill expands BCA's functions to manage programmes such as the Estate Upgrading Programme for private residential estates and the Enhancement for Active Seniors (Private Housing) programme, and expands URA's role to coordinate transport, utilities and other infrastructure planning. It also validates past fees and charges collected by BCA, HDB, NParks and URA, raises maximum penalties for wildlife feeding, and changes rules for professional registration and hybrid plants. The record does not set out the aggregate number of people affected or total sums involved in the validated fees.

key_points.point: The Bill contains 21 clauses and makes miscellaneous amendments to several Acts, largely technical and operational.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: The Statutes (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill contains 21 clauses and makes miscellaneous amendments to several Acts.

key_points.point: BCA will act as the Government's agent in managing programmes such as the Estate Upgrading Programme for private residential estates and the Enhancement for Active Seniors (Private Housing) programme.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: BCA will act as the Government's agent in managing programmes such as the Estate Upgrading Programme (EUP) for private residential estates and the Enhancement for Active Seniors (Private Housing) programme.

key_points.point: BCA will maintain foreshore structures belonging to the Government on state land allocated to MND.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: BCA will also take on the function of maintaining foreshore structures belonging to the Government and erected on any part of the foreshore that is state land allocated to the Ministry of National Development (MND).

key_points.point: BCA will provide administrative support to the Professional Engineers Board and Strata Titles Boards.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: BCA will provide administrative support to the Professional Engineers Board and Strata Titles Boards in the performance of their respective statutory functions.

key_points.point: URA will undertake and coordinate planning of infrastructure for transport, utilities and other infrastructure.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: URA will undertake and coordinate the planning of infrastructure for transport, utilities and other infrastructure in Singapore.

key_points.point: URA will provide administrative support to the Board of Architects, the Street and Building Names Board, and the Controller of Housing.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: URA will also provide administrative support to the Board of Architects and the Street and Building Names Board in the performance of their respective statutory functions as well as the Controller of Housing in relation to the administration of the Housing Developers (Control and Licensing) Act 1965 and the Sale of Commercial Properties Act 1979.

key_points.point: MND will move a Notice of Amendment at Committee stage to update the title of the SDCPA in clauses 2(e) and 20(11) when the Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Act 2026 comes into operation.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: MND will be moving a Notice of Amendment during the Committee stage to update the title of the SDCPA reflected in clauses 2(e) and 20(11) of the Bill when the Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Act 2026, which is passed but not in operation yet, comes into operation.

key_points.point: Clause 4(b) deletes Part 8C of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act 2020, which supported property developers facing COVID-19-related construction delays and allowed affected purchasers to seek partial reimbursement.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Clause 4(b) deletes Part 8C of the COTMA, which provided support to property developers who faced construction delays due to reasons related to COVID-19 and allowed affected purchasers to seek partial reimbursement from the developers for qualifying costs incurred due to the delay in delivery of possession.

key_points.point: Clause 4(c) deletes Part 10A of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act 2020, which facilitated cost-sharing between contractors and developers for foreign manpower cost increases due to COVID-19.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Clause 4(c) deletes Part 10A of the COTMA, which facilitated an equitable co-sharing between contractors and developers of increases in the cost of engaging foreign manpower due to COVID-19.

key_points.point: Clauses 7 and 8 allow the Board of Architects and Professional Engineers Board to recognise relevant pre-graduation internship and working experience for registration.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: These amendments allow the Board of Architects and Professional Engineers Board to recognise relevant pre-graduation internship and working experience as part of the practical experience required for registration as Professional Engineers and Architects.

key_points.point: Clauses 9 to 12 validate fees and charges collected by BCA, HDB, NParks and URA in the ordinary course of their operations.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: clauses 9 to 12 validate fees and charges collected by our Statutory Boards, namely BCA, HDB, NParks and URA in the ordinary course of their operations.

key_points.point: Subsidiary legislation to prescribe the fees has been made or will be made when the Bill is enacted.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: The necessary subsidiary legislation to prescribe the fees has either been made or will be made when this Bill is enacted to provide the agencies with the relevant powers and clear legal basis for the continued collection of these fees.

key_points.point: Clause 13 preserves court decisions and proceedings commenced before the First Reading of the Bill in relation to liability to pay the validated fees and charges.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Clause 13 provides that the validation of the fees and charges made by clauses 9 to 12 do not affect any decision or judgment of the Court given and any Court proceedings commenced before the First Reading of the Bill in relation to the liability of any person to pay any of those fees and charges.

key_points.point: Clause 14 increases the maximum licence period for the BCA Aggregate Importer's Licence from two years to five years.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Clause 14 amends section 31(5) of the BCA Act so that the maximum licence period for BCA Aggregate Importer's Licence is increased from the current two years to five years as a pro-enterprise measure.

key_points.point: Clauses 15 and 16 re-enact a 2017 amendment to the Building (Strata Management) Act 2004 so it can be brought into force in different stages, covering management fund use for social, cultural, sporting, legal and official manager purposes.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: These pertain to the use of management funds for social and cultural activities, sporting events, engaging legal services or remunerating an official manager where necessary.

key_points.point: Clause 17 expands the definition of scheduled species in the Endangered Species (Import and Export) Act 2006 to include hybrid plants.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Clause 17 expands the definition of "scheduled species" in the Endangered Species (Import and Export) Act 2006 (or ESA) to include hybrid plants.

key_points.point: Clause 17 empowers the Director-General of Wildlife Trade Control to inspect, analyse and certify both scheduled and non-scheduled species.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: clause 17 empowers the Director-General of Wildlife Trade Control to inspect, analyse and certify both scheduled and non-scheduled species.

key_points.point: Clause 18 allows HDB to recover charges and expenses for immobilisation, removal and storage of unlawfully parked or abandoned vehicles in HDB common property and open spaces.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: the amendments will expressly allow HDB to recover charges and expenses related to the immobilisation, removal and storage of unlawfully parked or abandoned vehicles in HDB common property and open spaces.

key_points.point: Clause 18 allows HDB to recover fees, charges, expenses and legal costs in vesting property under section 59 or compulsorily acquiring property under section 63(1).
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: HDB will also be allowed to recover fees, charges, expenses and legal costs incurred in vesting property in the HDB under section 59 of the Act or in compulsorily acquiring property for the reasons listed in section 63(1) of the Act.

key_points.point: Clause 19 raises maximum penalties for wildlife feeding offences under section 5A(3) of the Wildlife Act 1965.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Clause 19 raises the maximum penalties for wildlife feeding offences under section 5A(3) of the Wildlife Act 1965.

key_points.point: Imprisonment of up to 12 months may be imposed on repeat offenders for wildlife feeding.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Further, imprisonment for a term of up to 12 months may be imposed on repeat offenders.

key_points.point: Clause 20 provides updates to various Acts arising from the 2020 Revised Edition of Acts.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Clause 20 provides for the necessary updates to various Acts arising from the 2020 Revised Edition of Acts.

key_points.point: Ms Valerie Lee raised concern about the fairness of the 7 April 2026 cut-off date, which limits affected persons' ability to commence legal proceedings.
key_points.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee
key_points.quote: I am also concerned about the fairness of the cut-off date of 7 April 2026, which limits affected persons' ability to commence legal proceedings.

key_points.point: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik asked how BCA plans to partner with MCSTs to implement installation of fixtures under the EASE programme for private estates.
key_points.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
key_points.quote: How does BCA plan to partner with MCSTs to implement the installation of fixtures?

key_points.point: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik said the Bill does not clearly address who bears responsibility for estate maintenance and upkeep after EUP upgrading works are done.
key_points.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
key_points.quote: the Bill does not clearly address who bears responsibility for estate maintenance and upkeep after upgrading works are done.

key_points.point: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik asked whether existing safeguards apply equally to expenditures under the newly expanded MCST management fund scope.
key_points.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
key_points.quote: I would like to ask the Ministry whether these same safeguards apply equally to expenditures under the newly expanded scope.

key_points.point: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik asked whether there will be a cap on amounts clawed back from compensation payable to affected households in HDB compulsory acquisition.
key_points.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
key_points.quote: will there be a cap on the amount that may be clawed back from compensation payable to affected households.

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi asked for the aggregate quantum of sums validated under Part 4.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: what is the aggregate quantum of the sums being validated under Part 4?

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi asked on what legal basis each agency thought it had authority to impose the fees and charges.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: on what legal basis did each of these agencies think they had the authority to impose these fees and charges in the first place?

key_points.point: Mr Fadli Fawzi asked whether a cross-Government review was commissioned in response to the discovery that led to Part 4.
key_points.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
key_points.quote: has a cross-Government review been commissioned in response to the discovery that led to Part 4?

key_points.point: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim asked to what extent the amendments would materially expand BCA's ambit and how BCA's mandate would complement rather than overlap with existing agencies and town councils.
key_points.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
key_points.quote: to what extent would it materially expand BCA's ambit and how will BCA's mandate complement rather than overlap with the functions of existing agencies as well as town councils?

key_points.point: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim asked for the Ministry's renewed plans to partner with social service agencies to engage and educate the public, particularly seniors, about the dangers of feeding wild animals ahead of enforcement.
key_points.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
key_points.quote: Could the Senior Parliamentary Secretary please share the Ministry's renewed plans to partner with social service agencies to engage and educate the public, particularly seniors, about the dangers of feeding wild animals ahead of the enforcement?

key_points.point: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim asked whether any retrospectively validated fees were previously subject to legal challenge or adverse judicial comment.
key_points.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
key_points.quote: whether any of these retrospectively validated fees were previously subject of legal challenge or adverse judicial comment?

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe asked the Minister to clarify what quality of life means in the context of BCA's expanded role in private estates.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: I would like to ask the Minister if we could clarify what does quality of life?

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe asked whether URA's enhanced role will help agencies identify and prioritise accessibility gaps such as overhead bridges without lifts.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: will this help agencies, including LTA, where relevant, identify, prioritise such accessibility gaps more systematically, including overhead bridges without lifts?

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe asked whether the qualifying assessment will remain robust enough to assure the public that flexibility in pathways does not dilute professional standards.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: Will the qualifying assessment remain robust enough to assure the public that the flexibility in pathways does not mean dilution in professional standards?

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe asked how the Government will ensure ordinary individuals do not unknowingly break the law on hybrid plants.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: how will the Government ensure that ordinary individuals do not unknowingly break the law?

key_points.point: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre said Parliament is being asked to extinguish citizens' rights to challenge past fee collections in court for anyone who had not commenced proceedings before 7 April 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: we are also being asked to simultaneously extinguish citizens' rights to challenge those collections in court

key_points.point: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre said that if HDB was deducting administrative and legal costs from compensation without statutory authority, affected residents received less than the law entitled them to.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: If HDB was deducting its own administrative and legal costs from that compensation without statutory authority, then affected residents receive less than what the law entitled them to.

key_points.point: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre asked whether there will be refunds.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: will there be refunds?

key_points.point: Ms Elysa Chen said the amendments confer new statutory functions on BCA for upgrading programmes in private residential estates and expand URA's mandate to coordinate transport, utilities and other infrastructure planning.
key_points.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
key_points.quote: The amendments confer new statutory functions on BCA as the Government agency for upgrading programmes in private residential estates and expand URA's statutory mandate to coordinate not just land use but transport, utilities and other infrastructure planning.

key_points.point: Ms Elysa Chen said she strongly supports provisions formalising certification for endangered species and related products.
key_points.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
key_points.quote: I strongly support the provisions that formalise certification for endangered species and related products.

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said the fees were previously considered administrative fees and collected on a cost recovery basis, and that there is no refund to talk about because this is not a wrong collection.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: there is really no refund to talk about. Because this is not a wrong collection.

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said MND did the review together with the AGC.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: we did this review ourselves together with the AGC.

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said MND may not have the full accurate record of all amounts collected to share precisely.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: we may not have the full accurate record of all the amounts collected that we are able to share with them precisely.

key_points.point: Mr Chee Hong Tat said if MND can come up with the information subsequently, it will be happy to share it with Mr Pritam Singh and the House.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: if we are able to come up with the information subsequently, to the best of our ability, I think we will certainly be happy to share this with Mr Singh and with the House.

key_points.point: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi said he did not have the full number or extent of the collective amount asked for by Mr Pritam Singh.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: I do not have the full number, the extent of the collective amount as asked by Mr Pritam Singh.

key_points.point: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi gave an HDB fee range from $3.27 for renewal of an HDB Fire Insurance policy to $545 for an application for HDB's consent to sell a commercial property not under the lodgement scheme.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: In terms of the fees charged by HDB, the fees range from $3.27 for the renewal of a policy under the HDB Fire Insurance scheme for owners who default in renewing the policy, to $545 for an application for HDB's consent to sell a commercial property not under the lodgement scheme.

key_points.point: Mr Pritam Singh asked whether the Government has the number of people affected and the quantum of monies involved.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
key_points.quote: do you have the number of people affected and the quantum of monies we are talking about?

key_points.point: Mr Pritam Singh asked whether it was the AGC's position that collections before the First Reading of the Bill were illegal.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
key_points.quote: Was MND advised, after the review with AGC, was it the AGC's position that collections before the First Reading of the Bill were illegal?

key_points.point: Ms Sylvia Lim asked for clarification on the necessity for the retrospective legislation.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
key_points.quote: I have one clarification for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary, and that is on the necessity for the retrospective legislation.

key_points.point: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song asked for an order of magnitude of how many such fees were collected and the total quantum.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
key_points.quote: is there an order of magnitude that the Government can provide as to how many such fees were collected and what is the total quantum?

key_points.point: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song asked whether the Government is prepared to refund fees which he described as illegally collected.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
key_points.quote: is the Government prepared to refund these fees which were illegally collected?

key_points.point: The Second Reading question was put and the Ayes had it.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: I think the "Ayes" have it, the "Ayes" have it.

key_points.point: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi moved the amendment to clause 2 standing in the Minister's name.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Chairman, I move the amendment* to clause 2 standing in the Minister's name, as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

key_points.point: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi moved the amendment to clause 20 standing in the Minister's name.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Chairman, I move the amendment* to clause 20 standing in the Minister's name, as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

key_points.point: The Third Reading question was put.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: The question is, "That the Bill be now read a Third time".

key_points.point: Members stood for their dissent to be recorded.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: stood for their dissent to be recorded.

what_happens_next: The Bill was read a Second time, amendments to clauses 2 and 20 were moved in Committee, and the Bill was read a Third time; the Ayes had it. MND will move a Notice of Amendment at Committee stage to update the title of the SDCPA in clauses 2(e) and 20(11) when the Coastal Protection and Other Amendments Act 2026 comes into operation. Minister Chee said MND will try to share data on the quantum subsequently.
not_said: What was the aggregate quantum of fees and charges validated under Part 4, and over what period were they collected?
How many people were affected by each of the validated fee regimes?
On what legal basis did each agency understand it could impose the fees and charges before the Bill?
How and when did the Government first identify the issue that led to Part 4?
Whether a cross-Government review was commissioned, and if so, what was its scope and timeframe?
Whether other agencies, fee regimes or categories of collection may have similar legal uncertainty.
Whether refunds will be made, or a claims window provided, for past collections.
Whether safeguards such as approval thresholds or challenge avenues will apply to expanded MCST management fund uses.
How BCA will partner with MCSTs on EASE installations and what quality assurance mechanisms will apply.
Who bears responsibility for estate maintenance and upkeep after EUP upgrading works are completed.
Whether caps or statutory floors will apply to HDB deductions from compulsory acquisition compensation.
What public education or consumer guidance will accompany the inclusion of hybrid plants in the scheduled species definition.
Whether mandatory training for MCST council members will be introduced and what it will cover.
Whether data on warnings, prosecutions and custodial sentences for wildlife feeding will be published by age or profile.
Whether the qualifying assessment for architects and professional engineers will remain robust after recognising pre-graduation experience.
Whether the enhanced URA role will systematically identify accessibility gaps such as overhead bridges without lifts.
